statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across representative homepage, section, article, search, 404, and login-entry surfaces.

page.framework: Server-rendered MPA with Nuxt on article template
page.notes: Public news publisher. Representative coverage excludes video playback, games, newsletter submission, authenticated account management, and paid subscription completion because they are distinct products or require credentials.

paths.description: Homepage and primary news discovery template; audited because it is the main entry point and densest listing surface.
Politics section listing, representative of topic and category landing pages.
Current news article, representative of the core reading journey and article template.
Search results and a deliberately unmatched query, representative of content finding and empty-state recovery.
Invalid route, representative of HTTP error recovery.
Public login entry surface, checked for authentication affordances; the rendered endpoint exposed only branding in headless Chrome.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light screenshot, and computed styles report color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border, and media treatments.

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no view-transition usage on homepage or article templates; search and route changes swap abruptly.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route and major state changes with same-document or cross-document View Transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long news pages provide no position-aware reading or navigation cue.
findings.evidence: The 49,638 px mobile homepage and 13,694 px article expose static chrome with no scroll progress or scroll-state styles in the CSS feature probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware header treatment that preserves content space.

findings.summary: Interactive menus and search use custom controls rather than native overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: The rendered homepage has zero dialog, popover, and details elements while exposing expandable navigation and search UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover for transient menus/search and dialog only for modal flows, preserving native focus and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: The article template overflows horizontally on a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured scrollWidth 417 px against clientWidth 360 px, producing 57 px horizontal overflow on the core article path.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the fixed or minimum-width descendant, use intrinsic sizing, and enforce max-inline-size: 100% for media and embeds.

findings.summary: Reusable components rely on viewport breakpoints rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: The CSS/computed-style probe found no active container-type or @container usage across homepage cards and navigation components reused at different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type and focused @container rules for reusable cards and rails while retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Some mobile touch targets are too small or tightly spaced.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found eight target-size failures, including footer links only 14 px high with safe clickable spacing below 24 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas and spacing to at least the WCAG target-size floor without shrinking visible labels.

findings.summary: Search does not present a trustworthy empty-result state.
findings.evidence: A deliberately unmatched query returned an unrelated January article and no “no results” explanation, query suggestion, or recovery guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a clear zero-results state, preserve the query, offer spelling/category suggestions, and provide a direct retry action.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance misses the Core Web Vitals loading bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 5.7 s, LCP 8.6 s, Speed Index 6.3 s, and Time to Interactive 19.0 s; its performance score was 0.54.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image, reduce critical chains, and defer nonessential advertising, analytics, and media work until after primary content.

findings.summary: Heavy script work blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 3.9 s of main-thread work and 1.5 s JavaScript execution; the trace recorded four long tasks and 171 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, delay noncritical initialization, and load feature code only when its surface is used.

findings.summary: The critical network path is heavy and includes render-blocking resources.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 188 requests and 5,188,601 transferred bytes. Lighthouse found eight render-blocking requests with an estimated 1,240 ms saving and 1,524 KiB cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical dependency chain, prioritize only the LCP asset, self-host or streamline fonts, and apply durable cache headers to immutable assets.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused and duplicated client code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 545 KiB unused JavaScript and 38 KiB unused CSS; ag.core.js and core-app.js appear more than once in coverage results.
findings.suggestedFix: Split by feature, remove duplicate bundles, and avoid loading reCAPTCHA, identity, video, and ad code before the related UI is used.

findings.summary: Visible labels and accessible names disagree on multiple controls.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 12 label-content-name-mismatch failures even though generic button and link naming audits otherwise passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Make each accessible name include the visible label and remove conflicting aria-label text.

findings.summary: Touch reflow quality is reduced by undersized targets and article overflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found eight insufficient touch targets, and the 360 px article layout overflowed by 57 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix article reflow and enlarge mobile hit areas while preserving user scaling.

findings.summary: The homepage logs a browser error during a normal anonymous load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured “Not signed in with the identity provider” as a console error.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat anonymous identity state as expected control flow and avoid logging it as an error.

findings.summary: Browser platform hygiene has several avoidable failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated API, missing source maps for a large first-party script, an Inspector issue, and a BFCache blocker.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the deprecated API, publish valid source maps, resolve the Inspector issue, and remove the BFCache-blocking lifecycle behavior.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers showed no CSP or X-Content-Type-Options. Cookie audit found 17 cookies lacking Secure, many with SameSite=None, while HTTPS and HSTS were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, nosniff, and secure cookie defaults; use SameSite=Lax or Strict unless cross-site behavior is essential.

findings.summary: The anonymous homepage has a broad third-party and analytics footprint.
findings.evidence: Network evidence found 30 third-party origins and 186 of 188 requests classified off the main origin, with about 5.1 MB transferred outside www.foxnews.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate first-party subdomains in reporting, remove nonessential vendors, gate marketing tags on consent, and batch analytics.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: No CSP, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options was present; Permissions-Policy grants client-hint features but does not restrict sensitive capabilities.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy, nosniff, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy alongside CSP.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not proportionate for a long listing page.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 91 of 100 images without srcset, 94 legacy-format images, and 96 below-fold images without loading=lazy; Lighthouse estimated 613 KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP with responsive srcset/sizes and lazy-load below-fold images while preserving eager priority for the LCP image.

findings.summary: Background media and third-party code dominate page weight.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 5.19 MB total, including 1.94 MB media, 1.77 MB scripts, and 186 third-party requests; two autoplay videos had no controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop nonessential autoplay, defer media until visible or requested, and enforce budgets for advertising, identity, analytics, and recommendation code.

findings.summary: The homepage starts with a large memory footprint.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 640,199 nodes and 50,462,391 self-size bytes for a news listing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit retained objects by feature, remove duplicate initialization, cap caches, and defer heavy subsystems until used.

findings.summary: Repeated search toggling coincided with substantial retained heap growth.
findings.evidence: After ten search open/close cycles, heap self-size rose from 50.46 MB to 60.86 MB and node count from 640,199 to 690,822. Separate-load background variation lowers confidence, but the growth warrants retained-object analysis.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat the baseline/target/final snapshot sequence in one controlled session, then remove leaked listeners, DOM, timers, or caches identified by retaining paths.
